                                      PROPOSED ORDER

       This Order addresses the application of Southwestern Electric Power Company
(SWEPCO) for authority to amend its tariffs for retail service to include a new form Contract for
Electric Service – Large Load (ES-LL Contract) for the provision of electric service to new
customers with loads greater than 75 megawatts (MW). On September 15, 2026, the parties—
SWEPCO, Commission Staff, Texas Industrial Energy Consumers (TIEC), the Office of Public
Utility Counsel (OPUC), Cities Advocating Reasonable Deregulation (CARD), and Eastman
Chemical Company—entered into a comprehensive and unanimous agreement (the agreement).
The Commission approves the tariff including the ES-LL Contract, attached to the agreement as
attachment A, to the extent provided in this Order.

                                      I.   Findings of Fact
       The Commission makes the following findings of fact.

Applicant
1.     SWEPCO is a Delaware corporation registered with the Texas secretary of state under
       filing number 1211806.

2.     SWEPCO owns and operates for compensation in Texas facilities and equipment to
       generate, transmit, distribute, and sell electricity in Texas.

3.     SWEPCO holds certificate of convenience and necessity number 30151 to provide service
       to the public.

4.     SWEPCO operates solely outside of the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT)
       region.
 PUC Docket No. 58796                             Proposed Order                                  Page 2 of 13
SOAH Docket No. 473-26-07507


Application
5.       On October 3, 2025, SWEPCO filed an application for authority to amend its tariffs for
         retail service to include a new ES-LL Contract under PURA1 § 36.001 and 16 Texas
         Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.241.

6.       In its application, SWEPCO requested that its ES-LL Contract apply for the provision of
         electric service to new customers with loads greater than 75 MW.

7.       SWEPCO’s application does not propose any change to its existing rate schedules.

8.       SWEPCO’s existing Contract for Electric Service, Sheet No. VI-4, is not designed for the
         large loads expected to come online in SWEPCO’s Texas service area in the coming years.

9.       Adoption of SWEPCO’s proposed new ES-LL Contract is necessary to provide consistent
         and reasonable terms of service to new large load customers while ensuring existing
         customers and SWEPCO are protected against the risk of serving these large loads.

10.      In Order No. 2 filed on October 29, 2025, the Commission Administrative Law Judge
         (ALJ) found the application administratively complete.

Notice
11.      On October 3, 2025, SWEPCO provided notice of the application via email to all parties
         of record in SWEPCO’s last comprehensive base-rate proceeding, Docket No. 51415.2

12.      On or about October 3, 2025, SWEPCO provided notice of its application via publication
         on its website.

13.      On October 6, 2025, SWEPCO provided notice of its application with all of the
         municipalities that retain exclusive jurisdiction over SWEPCO’s rates and tariffs.

14.      In Order No. 2 filed on October 29, 2025, the Commission ALJ found SWEPCO’s notice
         sufficient.

Agreement
34.   On September 15, 2026, the parties entered into the agreement resolving the issues among
      themselves.

Agreement – Revisions to the ES-LL Contract
35.   Under the agreement, the Applicability section of the ES-LL Contract is revised to read as
      follows:
             This form of contract (CONTRACT FOR ELECTRIC SERVICE TEXAS
             – LARGE LOAD) shall apply to any customer whose Contract Capacity
             (per Schedule 1 below) for Computational load, whether new or incremental
             load, as of the date of the execution of this Contract by the Company and
             the Customer, is greater than or equal to 75 MW for any single
             Computational load facility or for multiple Computational loads in
             aggregate that should be considered a single facility for purposes of this
             Contract. “Computational load” means load that primarily consists of
             power-electronic-based load, specifically Computational load, such as data
             centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities.
             SWEPCO may exercise reasonable discretion in determining whether
             multiple Computational loads located in SWEPCO’s Texas service territory
             should be considered a single facility for the purpose of determining the
             applicability of this form of Contract based on any reasonable factor, such
             as whether the loads are controlled by the same ultimate entity, whether the
             loads constitute a single multi-building campus style development, and the
             number of interconnection points required to serve the requested load.
36.   Under the agreement, SWEPCO may exercise reasonable discretion in determining
      whether multiple Computational loads located in SWEPCO’s Texas service territory
      should be considered a single facility for the purpose of determining the applicability of
      the ES-LL Contract based on any reasonable factor, such as whether the loads are
      controlled by the same ultimate entity, whether the loads constitute a single multi-building
      campus style development, and the number of interconnection points required to serve the
      requested load.

37.   In the agreement, the parties agreed to the provisions specified in Findings of Fact 35 and
      36 as a compromise for purposes of this proceeding, given the specific large loads that have
 PUC Docket No. 58796                     Proposed Order                                 Page 7 of 13
SOAH Docket No. 473-26-07507


      approached SWEPCO, but acknowledged that the applicability of the ES-LL Contract is
      an issue that will continue to be evaluated in future proceedings and that SWEPCO may
      initiate a filing to address that applicability in the future, with the parties reserving their
      rights to take whatever positions they wish regarding any such application.

38.   Under the agreement, the Ramp Period section of the ES-LL Contract is revised to read as
      follows:
             The period beginning with the Beginning Date of Step 1 in Schedule 1 until
             the day prior to the Beginning Date of the last populated Step in Schedule 1,
             not to exceed five years.
39.   Under the agreement, the Initial Contract Term section of the ES-LL Contract is revised to
      read as follows:
             The period from the day this Contract is executed until eighteen years (18)
             from the inception of the Ramp Period.
40.   Under the agreement, the Minimum Billing Demand (kW) section of the ES-LL Contract
      is revised to read as follows:
             For purposes of calculating customer’s bill, during the Billing Period, the
             Billing Demand for each month shall be the greater of the Billing Demand
             as calculated in accordance with the “Determination of Kilowatts of Billing
             Demand” provision of the LLP rate schedule or 90% of the Contract
             Capacity stated in Schedule 1. Outside the Billing Period, the Minimum
             Billing Demand shall be 0 MW.
41.   Under the agreement, the Minimum Billing Energy (kWh) section of the ES-LL Contract
      is revised to read as follows:
             For purposes of calculating customer’s bill, during the Billing Period, the
             “Kilowatt-hour (kWh) Charge” (¢ per kWh) of the LLP rate schedule shall
             be multiplied times the greater of the actual kWh consumed in the billing
             period or the kWh computed as follows: Contract Capacity stated in
             Schedule 1 times 70% times billing hours in the month. Outside the Billing
             Period, the Minimum Billing Energy shall be 0 kWh.
42.   The agreement’s revisions to the ES-LL Contract are appropriate.

Agreement – Analysis, Reporting, Evaluation, and Tracking
43.   The parties agree that SWEPCO will collaborate with Commission Staff and other parties
      to determine and provide analysis, testimony, and supporting workpapers in future base
      rate case proceedings to address the following:
 PUC Docket No. 58796                   Proposed Order                               Page 8 of 13
SOAH Docket No. 473-26-07507


      a.     Cost-Shift Review: In SWEPCO’s next base rate case, SWEPCO agrees to include
             analyses of the costs it has incurred to serve new ES-LL Contract customers,
             whether those costs have been covered by incremental revenues from the ES-LL
             Contract customers, and whether any costs to serve ES-LL Contract customers have
             been shifted to other customers. SWEPCO will provide these analyses, including
             associated workpapers, in live format, and source documentation, in its application
             to facilitate discovery and review by the parties and the Commission. The parties
             reserve their rights to conduct discovery and take any position they wish regarding
             costs SWEPCO incurs to serve ES-LL Contract customers, and how ES-LL
             Contract customers should be treated from a ratemaking perspective, in the base
             rate case and any other appropriate proceeding. For purposes of this Cost-Shift
             Review provision, the term “ES-LL Contract customers” includes new and
             expanded Computational loads, as set forth in the Applicability section, to whom
             the parameters of the ES-LL Contract would apply regardless of which of
             SWEPCO’s jurisdictions the Computational load is located within.

      b.     Post-Base Rate Case Annual Report: SWEPCO will separately compile a report to
             be provided annually to the parties in this proceeding with the same categories of
             information on an ongoing basis for the period following SWEPCO’s next base rate
             case, during the interim period prior to SWEPCO’s subsequent base rate case, but
             after (1) a full twelve-month period following the first customer receiving service
             under this Contract; and (2) completion of at least Step 1 of Schedule 1. SWEPCO
             will provide these analyses, including associated workpapers, in live format, and
             source documentation, in its report to facilitate review by the parties and the
             Commission. For purposes of this provision, the term “ES-LL Contract customers”
             includes new loads to whom the parameters of the ES-LL Contract would apply.

      c.     Class Cost of Service Evaluation: In SWEPCO’s next base rate case, SWEPCO
             agrees to present two class cost of service and rate designs, one with ES-LL
             Contract customers as a separate class and the second with ES-LL customers within
             the LLP-Transmission class. Any party may propose alternative class cost of
             service and rate design approaches with respect to ES-LL Contract customers
 PUC Docket No. 58796                      Proposed Order                                 Page 9 of 13
SOAH Docket No. 473-26-07507


                during any of SWEPCO’s future base rate proceedings, as in the usual course. All
                parties reserve their rights to take whatever position they wish on these issues in
                future proceedings, including SWEPCO’s next base rate case.

      d.        Tracking ES-LL Revenues and Costs: SWEPCO agrees to track the non-fuel
                revenues received from the customers under the ES-LL Contracts, and the costs
                caused by those customers. The Commission will address the treatment of those
                revenues and costs in SWEPCO’s next base rate proceeding. The parties reserve
                their rights to take whatever positions they wish with respect to the proper treatment
                of those costs and revenues, as well as what constitutes a cost caused by an ES-LL
                Contract customer. For purposes of this provision, the term “ES-LL Contract
                customers” includes new and expanded Computational loads, as set forth in the
                Applicability section, to whom the parameters of the ES-LL Contract would apply
                regardless of which of SWEPCO’s jurisdictions the Computational load is located
                within.

44.   The agreement’s treatment of provisions related to cost-shift review, post-base rate case
      annual reports, class cost of service evaluation, and tracking of ES-LL revenues and costs
      is appropriate.

Agreement – CARD’s Rate Case Expenses
45.   On July 6, 2026, CARD filed the affidavit of Mr. Herrera, who attested that CARD’s rate
      case expenses from May 26 through June 30, 2026, in the amount of $30,685.50 for this
      proceeding are reasonable given the nature of CARD’s participation in this proceeding, the
      number of issues involved, and the complexity, importance, and scope of this docket.

46.   The rate-case expenses incurred by CARD from May 26 through June 30, 2026, in the
      amount of $30,685.50, are reasonable and proportionate to the nature and scope of this
      docket.

47.   In the agreement, the parties agreed that SWEPCO will reimburse CARD for their
      reasonable rate-case expenses incurred in this proceeding within 30 days of the date of this
      Order.
 PUC Docket No. 58796                      Proposed Order                             Page 10 of 13
SOAH Docket No. 473-26-07507


48.    In the agreement, the parties agreed that SWEPCO will seek recovery of CARD’s
       reasonable rate-case expenses incurred in this proceeding in a future proceeding.

49.    The agreement’s treatment of rate-case expenses is appropriate.

50.    It is reasonable for SWEPCO to reimburse CARD $30,685.50 for its rate-case expenses.

Effective Date
51.    In the application, SWEPCO proposed that the ES-LL Contract become effective on the
       date of the final order in this proceeding.

52.    On December 29, 2025, SWEPCO filed a request that its proposed ES-LL Contract become
       effective on February 2, 2026.

53.    On February 20, 2026, SWEPCO filed an agreed motion requesting that the effective date
       be extended from February 2, 2026 to December 17, 2026.

54.    In SOAH Order No. 5 filed on March 20, 2026, the SOAH ALJ granted the motion and
       “suspended” the “amended proposed effective date to December 17, 2026.”

55.    It is appropriate for the proposed ES-LL Contract to become effective on the date this Order
       is filed.

Informal Disposition
56.    More than 15 days have passed since completion of the notice provided in this docket.

57.    No person filed a protest.

58.    SWEPCO, Commission Staff, TIEC, OPUC, CARD, and Eastman are the only parties to
       this proceeding.

59.    No party currently requests a hearing, and no hearing is needed.

60.    This decision is not adverse to any party.

                                      II. Conclusions of Law
      The Commission makes the following conclusions of law.

1.    SWEPCO is a public utility as that term is defined in PURA § 11.004(1), an electric utility
      as that term is defined in PURA § 31.002(6), and a transmission and distribution utility as
      defined in PURA § 31.002(19).

2.    The Commission has authority over this proceeding under PURA §§ 14.001, 32.001, and
      36.001.

3.    SOAH exercised authority over this proceeding under PURA § 14.053 and Texas
      Government Code § 2003.049(b).

4.    The Commission processed this docket in accordance with the requirements of PURA, the
      Administrative Procedure Act,3 and Commission rules.

5.    The hearing on the merits was set and notice of the hearing was given in compliance with
      Texas Government Code §§ 2001.051 and 2001.052. The hearing was subsequently
      cancelled at the request of the parties.

6.    SWEPCO provided notice of its application in compliance with PURA § 36.103 and
      16 TAC § 22.51(a) and filed an affidavit attesting to the completion of notice in compliance
      with 16 TAC § 22.51(d).

7.    Under PURA § 33.001, each municipality in SWEPCO’s service area that has not ceded
      authority to the Commission has authority over SWEPCO’s application.

8.    Under PURA § 33.051, the Commission has authority over an appeal from a municipality’s
      rate proceeding in SWEPCO’s service area.

9.    The Commission’s consideration of the agreement complies with PURA § 14.054 and
      16 TAC § 22.206.

10.   The application, and the tariff proposed in the application, complies with PURA § 36.003
      and is not unreasonably discriminatory, preferential, or prejudicial.

11.    The rates charged to consumers continue to meet the requirements of PURA § 36.003
       because the amendment to SWEPCO’s tariff and the proposed ES-LL Contract approved

15.    The requirements for informal disposition under 16 TAC § 22.35 have been met in this

                                  III. Ordering Paragraphs
       In accordance with these findings of fact and conclusions of law, the Commission issues
the following orders.

1.     The Commission approves the tariff including the ES-LL Contract, attached to the
       agreement as attachment A, and to the extent provided in this Order, effective the date of
       this Order.

2.     Within 20 days of the date of this Order, SWEPCO must provide the Commission with a
       clean copy of the tariff pages approved by this Order to be stamped Approved and retained
       by Central Records. SWEPCO is further ordered to simultaneously notify Central Record
       of the documents to be stamped Approved.

3.     SWEPCO must reimburse CARD for its reasonable rate-case expenses incurred through
       the completion of this proceeding within 30 days of this Order.

4.     SWEPCO may seek the recovery of its rate-case expenses for this proceeding and for
       CARD’s rate-case expenses incurred through the completion of this proceeding in a future
       proceeding.

                                      PROPOSED ORDER

       This Order addresses the application of Southwestern Electric Power Company
(SWEPCO) for authority to amend its tariffs for retail service to include a new form Contract for
Electric Service - Large Load (ES-LL Contract) for the provision of electric service to new
customers with loads greater than 75 megawatts (MW). On September 15, 2026, the parties-
SWEPCO, Commission Staff, Texas Industrial Energy Consumers (TIEC), the Office of Public
Utility Counsel (OPUC), Cities Advocating Reasonable Deregulation (CARD), and Eastman
Chemical Company-entered into a comprehensive and unanimous agreement (the agreement).
The Commission approves the tariff including the ES-LL Contract, attached to the agreement as
attachment A, to the extent provided in this Order.

                                       I.   Findings of Fact
       The Commission makes the following findings of fact.

1.     SWEPCO is a Delaware corporation registered with the Texas secretary of state under
       filing number 1211806.

2.     SWEPCO owns and operates for compensation in Texas facilities and equipment to
       generate, transmit, distribute, and sell electricity in Texas.

3.     SWEPCO holds certificate of convenience and necessity number 30151 to provide service
       to the public.

4.     SWEPCO operates solely outside of the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT)
       region.

Application
5.       On October 3,2025, SWEPCO filed an application for authority to amend its tariffs for
         retail service to include a new ES-LL Contract under PURA1 § 36.001 and 16 Texas
         Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.241.

6.       In its application, SWEPCO requested that its ES-LL Contract apply for the provision of
         electric service to new customers with loads greater than 75 MW.

7.       SWEPCO' s application does not propose any change to its existing rate schedules.

8.       SWEPCO' s existing Contract for Electric Service, Sheet No. VI-4, is not designed for the
         large loads expected to come online in SWEPCO' s Texas service area in the coming years.

9.       Adoption of SWEPCO' s proposed new ES-LL Contract is necessary to provide consistent
         and reasonable terms of service to new large load customers while ensuring existing
         customers and SWEPCO are protected against the risk of serving these large loads.

Ajzreement - Revisions to the ES-LL Contract
35.    Under the agreement, the Applicability section of the ES-LL Contract is revised to read as
       follows:
              This form of contract (CONTRACT FOR ELECTRIC SERVICE TEXAS
              - LARGE LOAD) shall apply to any customer whose Contract Capacity
              (per Schedule 1 below) for Computational load, whether new or incremental
              load, as of the date of the execution of this Contract by the Company and
              the Customer, is greater than or equal to 75 MW for any single
              Computational load facility or for multiple Computational loads in
              aggregate that should be considered a single facility for purposes of this
              Contract. "Computational load" means load that primarily consists of
              power-electronic-based load, specifically Computational load, such as data
              centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities.
              SWEPCO may exercise reasonable discretion in determining whether
              multiple Computational loads located in SWEPCO' s Texas service territory
              should be considered a single facility for the purpose of determining the
              applicability of this form of Contract based on any reasonable factor, such
              as whether the loads are controlled by the same ultimate entity, whether the
              loads constitute a single multi-building campus style development, and the
              number of interconnection points required to serve the requested load.
36.    Under the agreement, SWEPCO may exercise reasonable discretion in determining
       whether multiple Computational loads located in SWEPCO' s Texas service territory
       should be considered a single facility for the purpose of determining the applicability of
       the ES-LL Contract based on any reasonable factor, such as whether the loads are
       controlled by the same ultimate entity, whether the loads constitute a single multi-building
       campus style development, and the number of interconnection points required to serve the
       requested load.

37.    In the agreement, the parties agreed to the provisions specified in Findings of Fact 35 and
       36 as a compromise for purposes ofthis proceeding, given the specific large loads that have

38.    Under the agreement, the Ramp Period section of the ES-LL Contract is revised to read as

              The period beginning with the Beginning Date of Step 1 in Schedule 1 until

39.    Under the agreement, the Initial Contract Term section of the ES-LL Contract is revised to
       read as follows:
              The period from the day this Contract is executed until eighteen years (18)
              from the inception of the Ramp Period.
40.    Under the agreement, the Minimum Billing Demand (kW) section of the ES-LL Contract
       is revised to read as follows:
              For purposes of calculating customer' s bill, during the Billing Period, the
              Billing Demand for each month shall be the greater of the Billing Demand
              as calculated in accordance with the "Determination of Kilowatts ofBilling
              Demand" provision of the LLP rate schedule or 90% of the Contract
              Capacity stated in Schedule 1. Outside the Billing Period, the Minimum
              Billing Demand shall be 0 MW.
41.    Under the agreement, the Minimum Billing Energy (kWh) section of the ES-LL Contract
       is revised to read as follows:
              For purposes of calculating customer' s bill, during the Billing Period, the
              "Kilowatt-hour (kWh) Charge" (¢ per kWh) of the LLP rate schedule shall
              be multiplied times the greater of the actual kWh consumed in the billing
              period or the kWh computed as follows: Contract Capacity stated in
              Schedule 1 times 70% times billing hours in the month. Outside the Billing
              Period, the Minimum Billing Energy shall be 0 kWh.
42.    The agreement' s revisions to the ES-LL Contract are appropriate.

43.    The parties agree that SWEPCO will collaborate with Commission Staff and other parties
       to determine and provide analysis, testimony, and supporting workpapers in future base
       rate case proceedings to address the following:

      a.     Cost-Shift Review: In SWEPCO' s next base rate case, SWEPCO agrees to include
             analyses of the costs it has incurred to serve new ES-LL Contract customers,
             whether those costs have been covered by incremental revenues from the ES-LL
             Contract customers, and whether any costs to serve ES-LL Contract customers have
             been shifted to other customers. SWEPCO will provide these analyses, including
             associated workpapers, in live format, and source documentation, in its application
             to facilitate discovery and review by the parties and the Commission. The parties
             reserve their rights to conduct discovery and take any position they wish regarding
             costs SWEPCO incurs to serve ES-LL Contract customers, and how ES-LL
             Contract customers should be treated from a ratemaking perspective, in the base
             rate case and any other appropriate proceeding. For purposes of this Cost-Shift
             Review provision, the term "ES-LL Contract customers" includes new and
             expanded Computational loads, as set forth in the Applicability section, to whom
             the parameters of the ES-LL Contract would apply regardless of which of
             SWEPCO' s jurisdictions the Computational load is located within.

      b.     Post-Base Rate Case Annual Report: SWEPCO will separately compile a report to
             be provided annually to the parties in this proceeding with the same categories of
             information on an ongoing basis for the period following SWEPCO' s next base rate
             case, during the interim period prior to SWEPCO' s subsequent base rate case, but
             after (1) a full twelve-month period following the first customer receiving service
             under this Contract; and (2) completion of at least Step 1 of Schedule 1. SWEPCO
             will provide these analyses, including associated workpapers, in live format, and
             source documentation, in its report to facilitate review by the parties and the
             Commission. For purposes ofthis provision, the term "ES-LL Contract customers"
             includes new loads to whom the parameters of the ES-LL Contract would apply.

      c.     Class Cost of Service Evaluation: In SWEPCO' s next base rate case, SWEPCO
             agrees to present two class cost of service and rate designs, one with ES-LL
             Contract customers as a separate class and the second with ES-LL customers within
             the LLP-Transmission class.    Any party may propose alternative class cost of
             service and rate design approaches with respect to ES-LL Contract customers
